newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses below peaks, dollar up on mark.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses below peaks, dollar up on mark.

text.p: Key European bourses failed to hold early record or near-record levels by mid-afternoon on Wednesday, with Paris dropping around three percent from its highs, largely on bad news on company taxes.
On the currency market, the dollar regained some strength after being hit by a rush into the yen following news of the flotation of the Thai baht.

It also advanced to a new 40-month high against the weak mark. "Breaking 1.75 marks was a tough nut to crack. We are above that level now and it should provide support," said a senior trader at a British investment bank.
But speculative selling sent gold to its lowest level since March 1993.

New records earlier in the day on the Frankfurt, Paris and Milan bourses, adding to a strong advance the previous day, were prompted by gains on Wall Street on Tuesday and strength in the dollar, good news for exporters.
But New York gave little lead on Wednesday, with the Dow Jones industrial average losing around a tenth of a percentage point after the first half hour of business.

The Paris bourse, having gained 1.4 percent to a new peak, took a big hit in late morning after government spokeswoman Catherine Trautmann confirmed that the new Socialist-led coalition was studying new company taxes.

"The prime minister recalled that if efforts are needed to promote solidarity and to contribute to economic recovery, then they should be shared by the different players in the economy -- public ones but also companies," she said after a weekly cabinet meeting.

Shares in Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel were briefly suspended limit-up after jumping more than 20 percent on news that France and Britain could extend its licence to 99 years. Eurotunnel was up 6.5 percent at 7.35 francs in mid-afternoon after an early high of 8.40.

The London stock market, Europe's biggest, had followed a 2.7 percent leap on Tuesday to rise within five points of its record level on the FTSE 100 index on the belief that it would get its wish for a tough first budget from the new Labour government to tackle inflation.
But, led by futures, it soon slid back in hectic and nervous trading ahead of the budget, due after a delay later in the afternoon.
"This is pure toss-of-the-coin trading," said one London trader. "The volatility has been outrageous."
The Treasury said the budget speech would be delayed by up to half an hour from the planned 1430 GMT start due to a parliamentary question on an alleged leak of information.
German shares ended bourse trade at a record close but the 30-share DAX index was below an earlier intra-day high.
"The pretty strong dollar has really given this market a fresh outlook," said one Frankfurt trader. "The outlook for now is for a consolidating tone before making another attempt to go higher.".
The British pound, which had reached a five-year high of 2.9100 on Tuesday, traded around 2.9060 marks ahead of the budget, up from 2.8880 at the previous close.
The mark retreated broadly after news that German industrial production fell 0.2 percent in May and more hints that the planned single European currency could be a soft one, dealers said.
The yen became a safe haven after the Bank of Thailand said it was dropping its pegged rates system against a basket of currencies and allowing the market to set rates.

"Whenever a developing currency is allowed to float, there is always some fear in the market and that causes a capital outflow, and in the Asian region the safe haven is obviously the yen," said Alessandra Stagliano, economist at Daiwa Europe.

"The fact Thailand has floated its currency could be the prelude to more countries moving, which would provide support for the yen, although that will take time to feed through," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International.
In reaction the dollar sank to a session low of 114.15 yen, although it later recovered as the surprise wore off, while staying below its previous European closing level.
Elsewhere, currency traders did not anticipate any change in interest rates from a meeting of the U.S. central bank's Federal Open Market Committee which ends on Wednesday, with news due at 1815 GMT.

"We don't see anything happening that might jolt the dollar out of its current range. There's no major influence coming from the FOMC and everybody seems comfortable with the dollar's recent range," Stagliano said.
Lyons said U.S. non-farm payrolls data, due on Thursday, could be of more interest to the market.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was at 114.35 yen and 1.7525 marks, compared with 114.90 and 1.7421 in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 3.1 points at 4,725.2, having earlier hit 4,791.1, just below its all-time high of 4,796.0 reached in mid-June.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was 46.80 points lower at 2,897.24 after an earlier record 2,986.09.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended bourse floor trade up 34.91 points at a new record close of 3,854.76 after an all-time record 3,871.13 earlier.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $332.15 an ounce in the afternoon, up from a 4-1/4 year low fixing of $331.45 in the morning but below $333.65 at Tuesday's London close. Silver was down one cent at $4.66.
